lines.text: If a woman on the beach asks you to hold her baby, don't.
My grandmother said that every winter in Shimane. I thought it was a story to keep kids off the rocks.
The night my boat broke down, I walked back along the shore. A woman was kneeling by the water, soaking wet, holding a bundle.
She asked me to hold her baby while she washed her hair. She smiled too wide.
The baby was cold. Then heavy. Then heavier. My arms wouldn't let go.
Behind her, something long slid out of the sea. It didn't stop coming.
It wasn't her hair she was washing. It was her body. Hundreds of meters of it.
I don't remember how I got free. I still have the bundle. It's a stone shaped like a baby, and it gets heavier every winter.
